accessibility_source_findings.finding: Single printable-character shortcuts ([, ], L) are global window listeners with no way to disable or remap them; they are suppressed only for INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable, not for a focused <select> (type-ahead with 'l' in the flight or target-layer select also toggles the layer panel).
role=tablist/tab without arrow-key navigation or roving tabindex; every tab is a tab stop. aria-controls points at one shared panel.
Left-rail module buttons expose the active module only through data-active (no aria-current/aria-pressed), unlike the investigation buttons beside them.
Measure/Buffer/Nearest tools, access-point selection for drawn points and imagery footprint identify are driven only by map click events; there is no keyboard or list alternative for drawn records.
A running query has no status region: while pending with no tokens nothing is announced or shown except the button text changing to STOP; streamed RAG text is not in a live region.
Pipeline state is conveyed by button label and inline colour only (no aria-live); failure text is appended to a log that is visible only in the Query tab.
2D/3D toggle and ProgramTimeline phase filter buttons carry no aria-pressed (state via data-on / class only).
Alert feed and contracts table headers have no scope attribute; Finance table uses role=grid on rows that are focusable individually without grid arrow-key navigation.
Investigation graph connector SVG has no role/label and node buttons are absolutely positioned by percentage; reading order is DOM order only.
No skip-to-content link; keyboard users traverse command bar and (when open) the whole left rail before reaching the module.
Timeline slider aria-valuetext is the raw cursor string, empty until data loads.

special_adjudications.question: 1. Display-name filtering against raw identifiers
special_adjudications.answer: The reported defect (Finance filter comparing only raw foreign keys) is fixed: a custom globalFilterFn builds its haystack from contract id, raw agency/vendor/site ids AND agency code/name, vendor name, site name, formatted amount, status and tier, and has tests. Residual mismatches of the same family remain in current source: (a) Finance column SORT still uses the raw accessor values for Agency, Vendor and Site while the cells render code/name, so header sorting orders by V-/A-/S- ids, not by the visible text; (b) the Nearest tool's result label prefers properties.id over properties.name, and the Sites target supplies both, so the user is shown a raw site id; (c) CSV export and the evidence-brief contracts table emit raw vendor/agency/site ids where the table shows names; (d) inspector linked-contract/anomaly lists and the watchlist show ids only. The ProgramTimeline search compares against the same title/detail/category/phase strings it renders (no mismatch). The Finance KPI cards and EXPORT CSV ignore the active filter.

special_adjudications.question: 2. Map layer loading that can remain stuck
special_adjudications.answer: The mechanism named in the old audit (whenStyleReady gated on map.isStyleLoaded) no longer exists; the runtime now resolves `ready` on the style.load event and layer hooks add sources directly. Loading is set at SI:255 (GeoJSON layers) and SI:326 (Martin vector layer); it is cleared by 'source-ready' (263/342), 'loaded' (267/352), 'error' (270/355, and 320 for tile errors) and 'idle' when toggled off (246/313). Paths on which it is NOT cleared: (1) hung request — both hooks use bare fetch with an AbortSignal but no timeout (257, 328), so a backend that accepts the connection and never answers leaves 'loading…' indefinitely; (2) abort/cancel — the catch and the post-await guards return without writing a status (260, 264, 269 / 341, 343, 354); when the cleanup is caused by a 2D→3D switch or a runtime reboot the effect re-runs with mapRef.current === null and returns at 236/303 before any onStatus call, so the last status ('loading…', 'source ready' or 'rendered') stays on the button for as long as 3D is active, and the layer buttons are still rendered in 3D (867-883) while the failure banner is 2D-only (848); (3) 'source-ready' is terminal if map.getSource(sourceId) is already true at 264/343; (4) two hooks write the same 'municipios' key: with Martin delivery the vector hook sets 'loading' and the disabled GeoJSON hook then sets 'idle' in the same commit (313 vs 246, declared at 477-496), so the button reads 'on' rather than 'loading…' until the fetch settles; (5) empty result — an empty FeatureCollection (backend returns one for any allowed layer with no file, main.py:472) is reported as 'rendered' with no empty indication; (6) vector layer 'loaded' is set when the source is added, not when tiles arrive, so missing tiles show 'rendered' unless MapLibre raises an error event carrying sourceId. Unmount is safe (state is discarded; cleanup aborts and removes layers, 275-279). Related flags with the same no-timeout weakness: gazetteer density (614-617) and the ERI catalog (spatial/imagery/eriApi.ts:65) which also suppresses URL-hash writes while loading (useImageryController.ts:135). Access-point registries use fetchWithTimeout but 'Records received; drawing…' never advances when the map is not ready (e.g. WebGL unavailable: activeMode stays 'maplibre' with ready=false, useSpatialRuntime.ts:60-70, so the panel is shown and the draw effect returns at useAccessPointsController.ts:121).

special_adjudications.question: 3. RAG stream termination without useful feedback
special_adjudications.answer: The silent-blank case is fixed in the client and covered by four tests: HTTP error → 'RAG backend returned <status>'; no body → 'returned no response stream'; done event with non-zero rc → 'RAG backend exited with code N'; rc 0 with no data lines → 'completed without producing output'; stream closed without a done event → 'ended without terminal status'; malformed done payload → 'invalid terminal status'; transport error/8 s header timeout → the exception text. Each calls onError then onDone, and QueryLayer renders a role=alert 'Query failed' card with the message plus a hint to switch to STUB; partial output stays visible below it. query_llm.py now exists at the repo root as a wrapper. What is still not useful: (a) the backend opens the subprocess with stderr=PIPE and never reads it, so the reason for a non-zero exit (traceback, missing model/dependency) never reaches the user — only the exit code does; an unread stderr pipe can also fill and block the child, in which case no done event is ever sent; (b) while pending and before the first token the panel shows nothing at all — no response card (needs streamLines.length > 0), no 'No query run yet' card (needs !pending) — only the button reading STOP; there is no overall timeout on the stream; (c) STOP/unmount only sets a cancelled flag: the fetch is not aborted and the generator has no cleanup to terminate the subprocess; (d) query_llm prints progress lines ('Loading model…', 'Retrieving relevant posts…', '====') to stdout, which are streamed to the user as answer text, and any one such line satisfies the 'produced output' check; (e) the error card persists after switching back to STUB until the next run.

special_adjudications.question: 4. Lazy-loading of heavy dependencies (must be preserved)
special_adjudications.answer: Exhaustive list of deferral points in non-test source: (1) six React.lazy module chunks in App.tsx — CommandCenter, FinanceIntelligence (defers @tanstack/react-table), SpatialIntelligence (defers maplibre-gl JS, the @turf/* packages, Zod-based imagery/access-point clients via its static imports), AnomalyWorkbench, InvestigationGraph, QueryLayer — rendered inside one Suspense with a 'Loading module…' fallback and a per-module ErrorBoundary; (2) one dynamic import, RuntimeFactory.createCesiumRuntime → './CesiumRegionalRuntime', which is the only file importing 'cesium' and 'cesium/Build/Cesium/Widgets/widgets.css', so Cesium JS+CSS load only when 3D is requested; (3) MapLibre's worker is imported with ?worker&url so it is a separate emitted asset; (4) Cesium Workers/Assets/ThirdParty/Widgets are copied to public/cesium by the postinstall script and fetched at runtime via CESIUM_BASE_URL='/cesium/'. There is NO manualChunks or any build/rollupOptions block in vite.config.ts — chunking is whatever Rollup derives from the dynamic imports. Caveats that affect what 'lazy' currently means: main.tsx statically imports 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css' and ten @fontsource CSS files, so MapLibre's CSS is in the entry CSS; InvestigationGraph statically imports AccessPointRelationships → accessPointsApi (Zod), and api/client.ts (entry) imports schemas/priis (Zod), so Zod is in the entry chunk; there is no graph library to defer — both graphs are hand-written SVG. Access-point relationships, the control cross-section, registry features and evidence are lazy at the data level (fetched on demand), not code-split.

special_adjudications.question: 5. Six modules; nothing reads the URL to select one; existing use of location.hash
special_adjudications.answer: Confirmed. ModuleId is the union command|finance|spatial|anomaly|graph|query; App holds it in useState initialised to 'command' and changes it only through setModule calls from the tab strip, the left rail, the command-bar submit (→ query), Command Center's OPEN QUERY LAYER button and its anomaly cards (→ anomaly). A grep of non-test source for location/history/URLSearchParams/hashchange/popstate finds no code that derives the module from the URL and no hashchange/popstate listener anywhere; the module is not persisted to localStorage either. The only URL consumers are in the Spatial imagery controller: it parses window.location.hash once at mount for map=zoom/lat/lng, eri, op, cmp, fp, base; rewrites the fragment with history.replaceState on moveend and on imagery state changes (skipped while the catalog is loading); and copies window.location.href for 'Copy link'. formatViewHash deletes only its own six keys and preserves any other fragment keys, and the viewHash header states the fragment is free because the app has no router — so a module key in the fragment would survive, but the Spatial controller only runs while the Spatial tab is mounted and its fragment remains in the address bar after leaving the tab. eriApi also reads window.location.origin, and the root ErrorBoundary calls window.location.reload().

special_adjudications.question: Where the frontend falls back to built-in mock data
special_adjudications.answer: One place: fetchPriisDataWithFallback catches any rejection from fetchPriisData (network error, 8 s timeout, or any non-2xx on any of the nine entity endpoints) and returns the bundled priisData with live=false. App also seeds its initial state with the same mock object before the fetch resolves. The only indicator is the command-bar text LIVE vs DEMO; the classification banner says DEMO in both cases. A Zod-invalid row is dropped by parseArray rather than triggering fallback, and an empty-but-reachable backend yields live=true with empty tables. Nothing else falls back to fixtures: spatial layers, imagery, access points, RAG and pipeline surface errors instead (spatial/accessPoints/fixtures.ts is imported only by tests).

denominator.coverage_statement: Exhaustive (every non-test file under server/frontend/src read or grepped, entry traced from index.html → main.tsx → App.tsx): the six modules, navigation items, chrome toggles, localStorage/URL settings, keyboard handlers, context-menu handlers (none exist), dynamic imports, and all FastAPI routes in main.py, eri_imagery.py, access_points_api.py, martin_ingress.py, production.py and desktop/app_server.py. Enumerated but not line-by-line read: spatial/accessPoints/accessPointLayers.ts, spatial/imagery/eriLayers.ts, components/Badges.tsx, schemas/priis.ts, the CSS files (only breakpoints/collapse rules checked), and the bodies of eri_imagery.py/access_points_api.py handlers (decorators and signatures only).
